_readme: Example taxonomy.json for the newsletter digest pipeline. This is a template with fictional entities, not a real watchlist — replace watchlist/frontier_labs/themes with your own tracked companies and topics. Keep the top-level shape (version, watchlist, frontier_labs, themes, selection_rules): newsletter_prefilter.py and newsletter_render.py read exactly these keys. NOTE: RSS/podcast feed sources are NOT configured here — they live in your scheduled-task prompt (or, if you've split them out per the repo README, in config/rss_sources.example.yaml). This file only drives story classification, not fetching.

frontier_labs._comment: Entities here are ALWAYS treated as subject_only by the prefilter script (see newsletter_prefilter.py build_alias_index) — they promote only when the lab itself is the subject of the story, not on a passing mention.

themes.name: Frontier technology developments
themes.definition: Major capability releases, performance milestones, or strategic moves by the leading labs/companies in your tracked field. Frontier-lab watchlist entries promote only when the lab is the subject of the story — a story centered on a frontier entity's own revenue, growth, or fundraising trajectory counts as subject-only, not just single-product announcements.

themes.name: Breakthrough technical or commercial milestones
themes.definition: Significant, verifiable technical or commercial milestones in your tracked domain (e.g. a validated performance record, a peer-reviewed result, a commercial deployment contract). HIGH BAR (see selection_rules.high_bar_themes) — promotes only for genuine breakthroughs, not routine funding, hiring, roadmap talk, conference appearances, or opinion pieces.

themes.name: Sector funding, deals & M&A
themes.definition: Funding rounds, contract/program awards, new entrants, valuations, and M&A in your tracked sector. Routine small-dollar activity should only promote above a size/significance threshold you define, not on dollar amount alone.

themes.name: Regulation & policy
themes.definition: Regulatory or legislative developments specific to your tracked domain. Promotes to Section 1 even without a named watchlist company, but only when the policy content is actually about your tracked domain — not general business/political news that merely mentions a watchlist company.

themes.name: Adoption & real-world integration
themes.definition: Real-world adoption, integration, or operational use of the tracked technology by organizations outside the frontier/watchlist set — e.g. a hospital, government agency, or enterprise deploying it at scale.

selection_rules._email_mode_note: two_section_audit includes both Section 1 (highlighted) and Section 2 (everything else) in digest.html/plaintext.txt. section1_only omits Section 2 from those two files. --md-dest from newsletter_render.py always gets both sections regardless of this setting.
selection_rules._theme_priority_order_note: Order Section 1 items within a topic by theme priority; themes not listed here sort last.

high_bar_themes.breakthrough-tech: Promote only for a genuine, significant, verifiable breakthrough (e.g. a validated record, a peer-reviewed result, a real commercial deployment contract) — NOT routine funding, hiring, roadmap talk, conference appearances, or opinion pieces. A named watchlist company/entity still auto-promotes on mention regardless of this bar; the high bar applies only to bare theme-keyword hits with no watchlist entity involved.

selection_rules._high_bar_themes_note: Generalized version of the original per-domain fields (e.g. fusion_significance_threshold, quantum_significance_threshold) into one map keyed by theme id, so you can add a high bar to any theme without adding a new field name each time.
selection_rules._drive_upload_mode_note: auto: attempt cloud-storage archive upload, retry once per file on failure, fall back to direct delivery for that file. always_manual: skip the archive upload entirely, always deliver via direct attachment. always_drive: attempt the archive upload with no fallback. Missing this key defaults to always_manual.
